title: Video Production and Motion Graphics | 22 Signals
description: Video production and motion graphics for brands that publish every week: reels, brand films, explainers, managed editing teams and live broadcast.
h1: Video production and motion graphics that keep up with your calendar
intro: 22 Signals offers video production and motion graphics for established companies that need content every week, not once a year: short-form video and reels, brand films, motion graphics, animated explainers, managed editing teams and live broadcast. One lead plans it, specialists make it, and every delivery date is agreed in writing before we start.

sections.h: The problem with video for most companies
p: Video now sits in every channel a buyer sees: the ad, the social feed, the sales deck, the website, the product page. Most companies still buy it the old way, one project at a time, from a studio that needs a fresh brief, a new quote and a month of lead time for each piece.

The result is a gap. Marketing needs twenty cuts a month and gets four. A product launch waits on an explainer. A good recording sits unused on a drive because nobody has time to edit it. Quality drops when the volume goes up, or the volume never goes up at all.
We set video up as a running service instead. The format list, the turnaround and the review steps are agreed once, so each new piece starts from a known standard instead of a blank page.

Motion graphics deserve a word of their own. Moving type, icons, charts and illustrated scenes let you explain a pricing model, a medical procedure or a software feature without a camera, an actor or a location. They are quick to update when a number or a screen changes, and they translate cleanly into other languages, which is why most of our recurring work mixes filmed footage with motion design.

sections.h: A motion graphics reel on us, for qualifying businesses
p: We would rather show you our work on your brand than send a generic showreel. For qualifying businesses only: after the 15-minute call, we make a short motion graphics reel with your own logo and assets, and send a note on how we made it.
The offer is for qualifying businesses, one reel per company. There is no purchase needed, and it is yours to keep whether or not we work together. Send the assets, and we take it from there.

sections.h: How a video project runs: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
p: Talk: we find out where the video will live, who it is for and what it needs to make them do. A 15-second paid social cut and a three-minute brand film are different jobs, and we price and plan them that way.

Plan: script or outline, references, style frames for motion work, a list of the cuts and formats you will receive, and a delivery date for each one, in writing. If filming is needed, we plan the shoot with you and agree how it will be crewed before any date is set.
Build: editing, motion design, sound, color and captions. You review at agreed points rather than at the very end, with comments collected in one place.
Grow: for ongoing work we track which videos perform on which channel and feed that back into the next batch. Hooks, lengths and formats change based on what your audience actually watches.

sections.h: Managed editing teams for weekly volume
p: Some brands publish so often that project-by-project video stops making sense. For them we run a managed editing team: editors and motion designers working to your brand rules, with a lead who checks every piece before it reaches you and a clear turnaround for each batch.

We run a managed video editing team of this kind for a US client today. The client sends footage and briefs, and gets back finished cuts on an agreed schedule, without hiring, training or managing editors themselves.

We have run and broadcast more than 20 large-scale live events, including live tournament broadcasts. The lesson from live work is simple: the date does not move. We bring that discipline to every deadline, recorded or live.
For live work we plan the run of show, graphics, overlays, replays and the online stream, and produce highlight cuts for social while the event is still running.

p: Our video team sits next to our paid media buyers, our 3D artists and our AI video specialists. A reel that wins on Meta can become a new ad set the same week. A product that does not exist yet can be shown with a 3D render. A presenter video can be versioned with AI and checked by a person. Few studios can offer that range under one accountable lead.

If you also need the campaign that runs the video, or the website it lives on, the same Signal Lead can bring those teams in without a second agency. And because live broadcast, editing and motion design are run by the same people, a single event can feed your channels for weeks: the stream, the highlight reel, the recap film and the clips for next year's promotion.

faqs.q: How fast can you turn around a reel?
faqs.a: We agree the delivery date in writing before we start, based on the brief, the length and the assets you have. Simple social cuts from existing footage are the quickest. Larger series get a schedule with a date for every batch, so your content calendar can be planned around real dates instead of hopes.

faqs.q: What do I need to send for the motion graphics reel?
faqs.a: Your logo files, brand colors and fonts if you have them, and any product images or footage you would like to see used. We go through them with you when we speak, and if your business qualifies, the reel follows with a short note on how we made it. There is one reel per company and no purchase is needed.

faqs.q: Do you provide ongoing video editing?
faqs.a: Yes. We run managed editing teams for brands that publish every week, with one lead, agreed brand rules and a set turnaround for every batch. You send footage and briefs, and you get finished cuts back on schedule. It suits companies that need the output of an in-house team without hiring and managing editors.

When a project needs filming, we plan the shoot with you and agree how it will be crewed before any date is set. Much of our work, though, is built from footage you already have, screen recordings, product assets and motion design, which keeps cost and lead time down. We will tell you honestly which approach suits the brief.

faqs.q: Do you use AI in video production?
faqs.a: Where it helps, yes: for presenters, backgrounds, versions and ad variations. Anything AI-generated is labeled, and every piece is reviewed by a person before it goes out. AI is a tool in the edit, not a replacement for it. Our AI video production page explains the approach in more detail.

faqs.q: What is the difference between video production and motion graphics?
faqs.a: Video production works with filmed footage: people, places and products on camera. Motion graphics are designed and animated: type, shapes, icons, charts and illustrated scenes. Most of what we deliver combines the two, for example a filmed founder message with animated captions and product callouts. Buying video production and motion graphics from one team keeps the style consistent across both.

Each cut in the sizes your channels need, usually vertical for Reels, TikTok and Shorts, square or vertical for feed ads, and widescreen for YouTube and your website. Captions come burned in or as separate files. Project files can be included when agreed in the scope, so another editor can pick up the work later.
